name: Battle of San Jacinto
kicker: Sam Houston’s 18-minute victory, 1836 · Won independence for Texas
briefing: On the afternoon of April 21, 1836, Sam Houston’s ragged Texian army charged across an open field into Santa Anna’s Mexican camp, shouting “Remember the Alamo! Remember Goliad!” The surprise attack was over in about 18 minutes. The next day, Texians captured Santa Anna, who was hiding in a common soldier’s clothes, and Texas won its independence from Mexico.

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Shortly before this battle, scout Erastus “Deaf” Smith and his men destroyed Vince’s Bridge, cutting off a route that either army might have used to escape or to bring in more troops.
tossups.r: Hours later, Sam Houston’s army attacked and defeated Santa Anna. For 10 points, name this April 21, 1836, battle that won Texas its independence.

tossups.p: As the Texian army advanced in this battle, a fife and drum played a popular love song, “Will You Come to the Bower?” A low rise in the prairie hid the advancing soldiers until they were close to the enemy camp.
tossups.r: Shouting “Remember the Alamo!” they routed Santa Anna’s army in about 18 minutes. For 10 points, name this 1836 battle.

tossups.p: A private named Mirabeau Lamar [“MEER-uh-boh luh-MAR”] rescued Secretary of War Thomas Rusk during a skirmish the day before this battle, and he was promoted to colonel to lead the cavalry in it. Lamar later became the second president of the Republic of Texas.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this battle in which Sam Houston defeated Santa Anna on April 21, 1836.

tossups.p: Juan Seguín [“seh-GEEN”], who later served as mayor of San Antonio, led a company of Tejano soldiers on the Texian side in this battle. Weeks earlier, he had left the Alamo as a messenger seeking help.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1836 battle where Sam Houston’s army defeated Santa Anna and won independence for Texas.

tossups.p: William Henry Huddle’s 1886 painting of the day after this battle, which hangs in the Texas Capitol, shows a wounded general lying under an oak tree as a captured enemy leader is brought before him.
tossups.r: That general was Sam Houston. For 10 points, name this April 1836 battle where Houston defeated Santa Anna.

tossups.p: On the morning of this battle, General Martín Perfecto de Cos [“KOHSS”] arrived with about 500 Mexican reinforcements, many of them tired from a long march. That afternoon, the Texians attacked the enlarged camp.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this battle in which Sam Houston’s army defeated Santa Anna in about 18 minutes.

tossups.p: Citizens of Cincinnati, Ohio, paid for two small cannons that were shipped to the Texian army before this battle. Those cannons, nicknamed the “Twin Sisters,” fired on the enemy during this battle, and what became of them after the Civil War is a mystery.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this April 21, 1836, battle where Sam Houston defeated Santa Anna and won Texas its independence.

tossups.p: Starting in 1948, the battleship USS _Texas_ was docked for decades beside the site of this battle, near a 567-foot monument topped by a giant star. That monument, finished in 1939, is taller than the Washington Monument.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1836 battle near present-day Houston, where Sam Houston defeated Santa Anna.

tossups.p: A legend that historians doubt claims that Emily West, a free Black woman in the Mexican camp, distracted the enemy general just before this battle and inspired the song “The Yellow Rose of Texas.”
tossups.r: In this battle, Sam Houston’s army shouted “Remember the Alamo!” For 10 points, name this April 1836 battle that ended the Texas Revolution.

tossups.p: After this battle, Vicente Filisola [“fee-lee-SOH-lah”] led most of the remaining Mexican army back toward the Rio Grande, obeying orders sent by his captured commander. Filisola, an Italian-born general, had been second-in-command of the Mexican army in Texas.
tossups.r: That commander, Santa Anna, later signed the Treaties of Velasco [“veh-LAHS-koh”]. For 10 points, name this 1836 battle that won independence for Texas.

tossups.p: Before this battle, the winning army spent about two weeks drilling at Groce’s plantation on the Brazos River, while frightened settlers fled east in the panic called the “Runaway Scrape.” Some of its officers grumbled that their commander would never stand and fight.
tossups.r: Sam Houston then turned and attacked Santa Anna. For 10 points, name this April 21, 1836, battle.

tossups.p: The winning general in this battle had a horse shot out from under him and was wounded in the ankle by a musket ball, but he stayed in command until the fighting ended. Weeks later, he sailed to New Orleans for treatment.
tossups.r: That general was Sam Houston. For 10 points, name this battle where Houston’s army defeated Santa Anna in about 18 minutes.

tossups.p: Months after this battle, the losing general traveled to Washington, D.C., where he met President Andrew Jackson in January 1837. As a prisoner, he had signed treaties promising to pull his troops back beyond the Rio Grande.
tossups.r: Texians had captured that general, Santa Anna, the day after this battle. For 10 points, name this April 1836 battle.

tossups.p: Augustus and John Allen founded a town on Buffalo Bayou months after this battle and named it for the battle’s winning general, who soon became the first elected president of the Republic of Texas.
tossups.r: That general was Sam Houston. For 10 points, name this 1836 battle where Houston defeated Santa Anna.

tossups.p: This battle took place on a plain where Buffalo Bayou meets a river, near present-day La Porte, Texas. The attack came in the middle of the afternoon, catching the enemy camp off guard while many soldiers rested.
tossups.r: The fighting lasted about 18 minutes. For 10 points, name this April 21, 1836, battle that won independence for Texas.

trap.title: Battle cry, not answer
trap.body: Tossups about this battle often mention the Alamo and Goliad, because Texian soldiers shouted “Remember the Alamo! Remember Goliad!” as they charged. A player who hears “Alamo” and blurts it out loses the question: the Alamo (February–March 1836) and Goliad (March 1836) were Texian defeats, while this battle on April 21, 1836, was the victory that won independence.
trap.fix: Sam Houston’s surprise attack, an 18-minute battle, the Twin Sisters cannons, and Santa Anna’s capture the next day mean San Jacinto. “Remember the Alamo” is the battle cry shouted here, not the answer.
trap.line: Real answer line: Battle of San Jacinto (prompt on Texas Revolution; do not accept “Alamo” or “Goliad”)
